nodes.name: Indicator chi_delta and its smoothings
nodes.statement: Given $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and ${\delta} \in (0,1/4)$, we define $\chi_{\delta}: [0,1) \to \mathbb R$ by \[ \chi_{\delta}(x):= \begin{cases}1 \ \text{ if } \ \|x\|\leqslant \delta \\[1ex] 0 \ \text{ if } \ \|x\|>\delta, \end{cases} \] and its continuous upper and lower approximations $\chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^\pm : [0,1)\to \mathbb R$ by \[ \chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^+(x): = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{\ if } \ \|x\|\leqslant \delta \\[1ex] 1+ \dfrac{1}{\delta\varepsilon}(\delta-\|x\|) &\text{\ if } \ \delta < \|x\| \leqslant (1+\varepsilon)\delta \\[1.3ex] 0 & \text{\ if } \ \|x\|>(1+\varepsilon)\delta \end{cases} \] and $$ \chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^-(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{\ if } \ \|x\|\leqslant (1 -\varepsilon)\delta \\[1ex] \dfrac{1}{\delta\varepsilon}(\delta-\|x\|) &\text{\ if } \ (1-\varepsilon)\delta < \|x\| \leqslant \delta \\[1.3ex] 0 & \text{\ if } \ \|x\|>\delta. \end{cases} $$

nodes.name: Two-dimensional target functions W^pm
nodes.statement: Given a real positive function $\psi:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow [0,1)$ and an integer $q\geqslant 4$, we define $W_{q,\varepsilon}^{+}, W_{q,\varepsilon}^{-}: [0,1)^2\to\mathbb R$ by \vspace{2mm} \begin{equation*} W_{q,\varepsilon}^{+}({\alpha},\gamma) :=\ \sum_{p=0}^{q-1}\chi_{\frac{\psi(q)}{q}, \varepsilon}^{+}\left(\textstyle{{\alpha}- \frac{p+\gamma}{q}}\right) \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} W_{q,\varepsilon}^{-}({\alpha},\gamma) :=\sum_{p=0}^{q-1}\chi_{\frac{\psi(q)}{q}, \varepsilon}^{-}\left(\textstyle{{\alpha}- \frac{p+\gamma}{q}}\right) \, . \vspace{2mm} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Notation W^pm
nodes.statement: In the sequel, we write $ W_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}$ to mean both the `upper' and `lower' functions, when this creates no risk of confusion.

nodes.name: Notation chi^pm
nodes.statement: Similarly we write $\chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^{\pm}$ to refer to both $\chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^{+}$ and $\chi_{\delta, \varepsilon}^{-}$.

nodes.name: Suppressing psi from W
nodes.statement: As $\psi$ is considered fixed, we write $W_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}$ instead of the more descriptive $W_{q,\varepsilon, \psi}^{\pm}$.

nodes.name: Sandwich of nu(E_t) by W integrals
Equation (6.5)
nodes.label: muineq

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients of chi and W
nodes.statement: For $\mathbf{k} = (k_1,k_2) \in \mathbb Z$ let $ \widehat{\chi}_{\delta, \varepsilon}^{\pm}(\mathbf{k})$ and $\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(\mathbf{k})$ denote the $\mathbf{k}^{\mathrm{th}}$ Fourier coefficient of $ {\chi}_{\delta, \varepsilon}^{\pm} $ and $ {W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm},$ respectively.

nodes.name: Coefficient A(q,k_1)
nodes.statement: We denote \[ A(q,k_1):=\dfrac{q\left(\cos(2\pi k_1\psi(q)q^{-1})-\cos(2\pi k_1\psi(q)q^{-1}(1+\varepsilon))\right)}{2\pi^2 k_1^2\psi(q)q^{-1}\varepsilon}. \]

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients of W^+
nodes.statement:
Using \cite[Equation (46)]{PVZZ2022} we compute, for $k_1
eq 0$, that  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} &\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^+(k_1,k_2)\, = \int_0^1\int_0^1 W_{q,\varepsilon}^{+}({\alpha},\gamma) e\left(-k_1 {\alpha} -k_2\gamma)ight) \mathrm d {\alpha} \mathrm d\gamma \&= \, egin{cases} \int_0^1 e\left( \dfrac{-k_1 \gamma}{ q}- k_2\gammaight) A(q,k_1)\mathrm d\gamma, &	ext{if } q \mid k_1 \[3ex] 0, &	ext{if } q
mid k_1 \end{cases} \&= \, egin{cases} A(q,k_1), &	ext{if } k_1=-q k_2 \[3ex] 0, &	ext{if } k_1
eq - q k_2. \end{cases} \end{aligned} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (6.6)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^+(k_1,k_2)\, = \int_0^1\int_0^1 W_{q,\varepsilon}^{+}({\alpha},\gamma) e\left(-k_1 {\alpha} -k_2\gamma)\right) \mathrm d {\alpha} \mathrm d\gamma \\&= \,\begin{cases} \int_0^1 e\left( \dfrac{-k_1 \gamma}{ q}- k_2\gamma\right) A(q,k_1)\mathrm d\gamma, &\text{if } q \mid k_1 \\[3ex] 0, &\text{if } q\nmid k_1 \end{cases} \\&= \,\begin{cases} A(q,k_1), &\text{if } k_1=-q k_2 \\[3ex] 0, &\text{if } k_1\neq - q k_2. \end{cases} \end{aligned}
nodes.label: fcoef

nodes.name: Zero-frequency coefficients of W^+
nodes.statement: We also find that \begin{equation} \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{+}(0,0)=(2+\varepsilon) \psi(q) \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{+}(0,k_2)=0 \qquad (k_2 \ne 0). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (6.7)
nodes.statement: \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{+}(0,0)=(2+\varepsilon) \psi(q)
nodes.label: fcoef_zero

nodes.name: Equation (6.8)
nodes.statement: \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{+}(0,k_2)=0 \qquad (k_2 \ne 0).
nodes.label: fcoef_zero_nonzero

nodes.name: Coefficient B(q,k_1)
nodes.statement: We denote \[ B(q,k_1):=\dfrac{q\left(\cos(2\pi k_1\psi(q)q^{-1}(1-\varepsilon))-\cos(2\pi k_1\psi(q)q^{-1}) \right)}{2\pi^2 k_1^2\psi(q)q^{-1}\varepsilon}. \]

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients of W^-
nodes.statement: For $k_1\neq 0$, we have \begin{equation} \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^-(k_1,k_2)\, =\, \begin{cases} B(q,k_1) &\text{\ if } k_1= - q k_2 \\[3ex] 0 & \text{\ if } k_1\neq - q k_2. \end{cases} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (6.9)
nodes.statement: \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^-(k_1,k_2)\, =\, \begin{cases} B(q,k_1) &\text{\ if } k_1= - q k_2 \\[3ex] 0 & \text{\ if } k_1\neq - q k_2. \end{cases}
nodes.label: fcoef2

nodes.name: Zero-frequency coefficients of W^-
nodes.statement: We also find that \begin{equation} \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^-(0,0) = (2 - \varepsilon)\, \psi(q) \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^-(0,k_2) = 0 \qquad (k_2 \ne 0). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (6.10)
nodes.statement: \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^-(0,0) = (2 - \varepsilon)\, \psi(q)
nodes.label: fcoef_zero2

nodes.name: Equation (6.11)
nodes.statement: \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^-(0,k_2) = 0 \qquad (k_2 \ne 0).
nodes.label: fcoef_zero_nonzero2

nodes.name: Proof of (6.12)
nodes.statement: Now $\sum\limits_{\mathbf{k} \in \mathbb Z^2}| \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(\mathbf{k} ) | < \infty $, so the Fourier series \[ \sum_{\mathbf{k} \in \mathbb Z^2}\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(\mathbf{k}) e( k_1 {\alpha} + k_2 \gamma ) \] converges uniformly to $W_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}({\alpha},\gamma)$ for all $({\alpha},\gamma) \in [0,1)^2$. It follows that \begin{eqnarray*} \int_0^1 W_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}({\alpha},\gamma) \; \mathrm{d}\nu({\alpha},\gamma) \; = \; \sum_{\mathbf{k}\in \mathbb Z^2} \, \widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(\mathbf{k}) \; \widehat{\nu}(-\mathbf{k}) \, . \end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Absolute convergence of the Fourier series of $W^\pm$ gives Parseval-type integration against $\nu$.

nodes.name: Fourier bounds for nu(E_t)
Equation (6.12)
nodes.label: mu_ie

nodes.name: Bounds on Fourier coefficients of W
nodes.statement: The arguments leading to \cite[Equations (51) and (52)]{PVZZ2022} can be used to deduce from~\eqref{fcoef} and~\eqref{fcoef2} the inequalities \begin{eqnarray} |\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(qk_2,-k_2)| &\leqslant& (2+\varepsilon) \, \psi(q), \\ |\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(q k_2,-k_2)| &\leqslant& \frac{1}{\pi^2k_2^2\psi(q)\varepsilon} , \end{eqnarray} valid for any integer $k_2\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Equation (6.13)
nodes.statement: |\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(qk_2,-k_2)| &\leqslant& (2+\varepsilon) \, \psi(q),
nodes.label: ub_Wpm_zero

nodes.name: Equation (6.14)
nodes.statement: |\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(q k_2,-k_2)| &\leqslant& \frac{1}{\pi^2k_2^2\psi(q)\varepsilon} ,
nodes.label: ub_Wpm_nonzero

nodes.name: Sums of Fourier coefficients of W
nodes.statement: Let $0< \varepsilon,\tilde{\varepsilon} \leqslant 1$. Then, for any integers $q, r \geqslant 4$, we have \begin{equation} \sum_{s \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big| \ < \ \frac{12}{\varepsilon^{1/2}} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \sum_{s\in \mathbb Z} \sum_{t\in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s) \widehat{W}_{r,\tilde{\varepsilon}}^{\pm}(tr,-r)\big| \ \leqslant \ \frac{144}{\varepsilon^{1/2}\cdot\tilde{\varepsilon}^{1/2}} \, . \end{equation}
nodes.label: main_part_bounded

nodes.name: Equation (6.15)
nodes.statement: \sum_{s \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big| \ < \ \frac{12}{\varepsilon^{1/2}}
nodes.label: ub_single_sum

nodes.name: Equation (6.16)
nodes.statement: \sum_{s\in \mathbb Z} \sum_{t\in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s) \widehat{W}_{r,\tilde{\varepsilon}}^{\pm}(tr,-r)\big| \ \leqslant \ \frac{144}{\varepsilon^{1/2}\cdot\tilde{\varepsilon}^{1/2}} \, .
nodes.label: ub_double_sum

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} &\sum_{s \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big| \\ &= \sum_{|s| \leqslant \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi\psi(q)\varepsilon^{1/2}}} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big| + \sum_{|s| > \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi\psi(q) \varepsilon^{1/2}}} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big|. \end{align*} Using \eqref{fcoef_zero} and \eqref{W_ub_psi} in the first sum and \eqref{W_ub_1s2} in the second, we obtain \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \sum_{s \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big| &\leqslant \: 3 \sum_{|s| \leqslant \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi\psi(q) \varepsilon^{1/2}}} \hspace{-5mm} \psi(q) \ \ + \hspace*{3ex} \sum_{|s| > \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi\psi(q) \varepsilon^{1/2}}} \frac{1}{\pi^2 s^2\psi(q)\varepsilon} \\ &\leqslant \: \frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{\pi\varepsilon^{1/2}} \ + 3\psi(q) + \ \frac{ 2 \sqrt{2}}{\pi\varepsilon^{1/2}} + 6\psi(q) \ < \ \frac{12}{\varepsilon^{1/2}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation*} The inequality \eqref{ub_double_sum} follows from \eqref{ub_single_sum} and the fact that \begin{align*} &\sum_{s\in \mathbb Z} \sum_{t\in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\widehat{W}_{r,\tilde{\varepsilon}}^{\pm}(tr,-r)\big| \\ &= \Big(\sum_{s \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big|\Big) \Big(\sum_{t \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{r,\tilde{\varepsilon}}^{\pm}(tr,-r)\big|\Big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split the sum at the threshold where the two coefficient bounds cross.

nodes.name: Split the sum
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align*} &\sum_{s \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big| \\ &= \sum_{|s| \leqslant \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi\psi(q)\varepsilon^{1/2}}} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big| + \sum_{|s| > \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi\psi(q) \varepsilon^{1/2}}} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big|. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split at $|s|\approx 1/(\psi(q)\varepsilon^{1/2})$.

nodes.name: Bound both ranges
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{fcoef_zero} and \eqref{W_ub_psi} in the first sum and \eqref{W_ub_1s2} in the second, we obtain \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \sum_{s \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big| &\leqslant \: 3 \sum_{|s| \leqslant \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi\psi(q) \varepsilon^{1/2}}} \hspace{-5mm} \psi(q) \ \ + \hspace*{3ex} \sum_{|s| > \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi\psi(q) \varepsilon^{1/2}}} \frac{1}{\pi^2 s^2\psi(q)\varepsilon} \\ &\leqslant \: \frac{3 \sqrt{2}}{\pi\varepsilon^{1/2}} \ + 3\psi(q) + \ \frac{ 2 \sqrt{2}}{\pi\varepsilon^{1/2}} + 6\psi(q) \ < \ \frac{12}{\varepsilon^{1/2}}. \end{aligned} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Use (6.6), (6.13) on small $s$ and (6.14) on large $s$.

nodes.name: Double sum
nodes.statement: The inequality \eqref{ub_double_sum} follows from \eqref{ub_single_sum} and the fact that \begin{align*} &\sum_{s\in \mathbb Z} \sum_{t\in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\widehat{W}_{r,\tilde{\varepsilon}}^{\pm}(tr,-r)\big| \\ &= \Big(\sum_{s \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{q,\varepsilon}^{\pm}(sq,-s)\big|\Big) \Big(\sum_{t \in \mathbb Z} \big|\widehat{W}_{r,\tilde{\varepsilon}}^{\pm}(tr,-r)\big|\Big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The double sum factorises.

nodes.name: Upper bounds for nu(E_t)
assumptions: $\nu$ be a probability measure supported on a subset $F$ of $[0,1)^2$
nodes.label: lem2

nodes.name: Equation (6.17)
nodes.statement: \nu(\mathcal E_{t}) &\leqslant& 3\psi(n_t) + 12 \max_{k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}}|\widehat{\nu}(-k n_t,k)| ,
nodes.label: lem2_result1

nodes.name: Equation (6.18)
nodes.statement: \nu(\mathcal E_{t}) &\leqslant& 3\psi(n_t) + 2\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{|\widehat{\nu}(-k n_t,k)|}{k}.
nodes.label: lem2_result2

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.4
nodes.statement_short: Apply (6.12) with $\varepsilon=1$ and the coefficient bounds of Lemma 6.3.

nodes.name: Fourier expansion with eps=1
nodes.statement: It follows from \eqref{mu_ie} with $\varepsilon= 1$, and \eqref{fcoef}, that \begin{equation} \nu(\mathcal E_{t}) \ \leqslant \ 3\psi(n_t) + \sum_{k \in \mathbb Z \setminus \{0 \} }\widehat{W}_{n_t,1}^{+}(k n_t, -k) \ \widehat{\nu}(-k n_t, k). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Apply (6.12) with $\varepsilon=1$ and (6.5).

nodes.name: Equation (6.19)
nodes.statement: \nu(\mathcal E_{t}) \ \leqslant \ 3\psi(n_t) + \sum_{k \in \mathbb Z \setminus \{0 \} }\widehat{W}_{n_t,1}^{+}(k n_t, -k) \ \widehat{\nu}(-k n_t, k).
nodes.label: lem2_ie2

nodes.name: First bound
nodes.statement: The desired estimate~\eqref{lem2_result1} now immediately follows from this, together with the fact that by Lemma~\ref{main_part_bounded}, \begin{equation*} \Big|\sum_{k \in \mathbb Z \setminus \{0 \} }\widehat{W}_{n_t,1}^{+}(k n_t, -k) \ \widehat{\nu}(-k n_t,k)\Big| \ \stackrel{\eqref{ub_single_sum}}{\leqslant} \ 12 \, \max_{k\in\mathbb Z\setminus \{0\} }|\widehat{\nu}(-k n_t,k)|. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 6.3 gives (6.17).

nodes.name: Equation lem2_ie3
nodes.statement: \Big|\sum_{k \in \mathbb Z \setminus \{0 \} }\widehat{W}_{n_t,1}^{+}(k n_t, -k) \ \widehat{\nu}(-k n_t,k)\Big| \ \stackrel{\eqref{ub_single_sum}}{\leqslant} \ 12 \, \max_{k\in\mathbb Z\setminus \{0\} }|\widehat{\nu}(-k n_t,k)|.
nodes.label: lem2_ie3

nodes.name: Geometric mean
nodes.statement: To prove \eqref{lem2_result2}, note that the geometric mean of the inequalities~\eqref{W_ub_psi} and~\eqref{W_ub_1s2} implies that, for every $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, $$ \big|\widehat{W}_{n_t,1}^{\pm}(k n_t,-k)\big| \ \leqslant \ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\pi |k|} \ \leqslant \ \frac{1}{|k|}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Geometric mean of (6.13) and (6.14) gives $|\widehat W|\le 1/|k|$.

nodes.name: Second bound
nodes.statement: This and \eqref{lem2_ie2} imply \eqref{lem2_result2}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude (6.18).

nodes.name: Convergence theorem for lacunary approximation
nodes.statement_short: If the Fourier coefficients of $\nu$ are summable along the relevant lattice and $\sum\psi(n_t)<\infty$, then $\nu(\mathcal W(\psi))=0$.
nodes.label: mainCONV

nodes.name: Equation (6.20)
nodes.statement: \sum_{t=1}^{\infty} \; \max_{k\in\mathbb Z \setminus \{ 0\} }|\widehat{\nu}(-k n_t,k)|< \infty,
nodes.label: cond2_2

nodes.name: Equation (6.21)
nodes.statement: \sum_{t=1}^{\infty} \, \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z \setminus \{ 0\} } \frac{|\widehat{\nu} (-kn_t,k)|}{|k|} < \infty .
nodes.label: cond2

nodes.name: Equation (6.22)
nodes.statement: \sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty}\psi(n_t)< \infty.
nodes.label: convergence

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.5
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma~\ref{lem2} and hypotheses~\eqref{cond2_2} and~\eqref{cond2} of the theorem that \[ \sum\limits_{t=1}^{\infty}\nu(\mathcal E_t)<\infty. \] The result now follows from the first Borel--Cantelli lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 6.4 and the first Borel-Cantelli lemma.

nodes.name: Convergence case of the counting theorem
nodes.statement: Note that the condition \eqref{LogDecay} implies \eqref{cond2_2}, as well as \eqref{cond2}. Thus, if we have~\eqref{convergence}, then it follows from Theorem~\ref{mainCONV} that \[ \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N) \ll 1, \] for $\nu$-almost all $(\alpha,\gamma)$. At the same time, under \eqref{convergence}, the right-hand side of~\eqref{countlacresult} is also bounded. We thereby obtain the conclusion of Theorem \ref{GeneralCountingThm} under the assumption \eqref{convergence}. We may therefore assume for the remainder of this section that \begin{equation*} \sum_{t=1}^\infty \psi(n_t) = \infty. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Equation divergence
nodes.statement: \sum_{t=1}^\infty \psi(n_t) = \infty.
nodes.label: divergence

nodes.name: Reduction to psi(n_t) at least t^{-tau}
nodes.statement: We work within the framework of Theorem~\ref{thm_lacunary}. Let $\tau>1$, let $\psi_\tau: \mathbb N \to [0,1)$ be any function such that \[ \psi_\tau(n_t) = t^{-\tau} \qquad (t \in \mathbb N), \] and put $\widetilde{\psi} = \max \{ \psi, \psi_\tau \}$. Then, for $\nu$-almost all pairs $({\alpha}, {\gamma})$, the formula \eqref{countlacresult} for $\psi$ is equivalent to the same formula with $\psi$ replaced by $\widetilde{\psi}$. In particular, when proving Theorem \ref{thm_lacunary}, we may assume that \begin{equation*} \psi(n_t) \geqslant t^{-\tau} \qquad (t \in \mathbb N). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Replacing $\psi$ by $\max\{\psi,\psi_\tau\}$ does not change the counting formula almost surely.
assumptions: Let $\tau>1$, let $\psi_\tau: \mathbb N \to [0,1)$ be any function such that \[ \psi_\tau(n_t) = t^{-\tau} \qquad (t \in \mathbb N),
conclusions: for $\nu$-almost all pairs $({\alpha}, {\gamma})$, the formula \eqref{countlacresult} for $\psi$ is equivalent to the same formula with $\psi$ replaced by $\widetilde{\psi}$.
nodes.label: cor_min_psi

nodes.name: Equation psi_is_not_small
nodes.statement: \psi(n_t) \geqslant t^{-\tau} \qquad (t \in \mathbb N).
nodes.label: psi_is_not_small

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6.7
nodes.statement:
It follows from the definition~\eqref{def_cN} of the function $\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)$ that \[ \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)\leqslant \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\widetilde{\psi},N)\leqslant \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)+\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{	au},N) \] At the same time, it follows from~Theorem~ef{mainCONV} that, for $
u$-almost all pairs $({\alpha},{\gamma})$, we have $({\alpha}, {\gamma}) 
otin \mathcal W(\psi_{	au})$, which is equivalent to \[ \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{	au},N) \ll 1, \] Thus, $
u$-almost surely, \[ \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\widetilde{\psi},N)=\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{	au},N) + O(1). \] For these pairs $(\alpha, {\gamma})$, when we change $\psi$ to $\widetilde{\psi}$, we modify the left-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult} by $O(1)$. Similarly, using the notation $\widetilde{\Psi}:=\sum_{t \leqslant N} \widetilde{\psi}(n_t)$, we have \[ \Psi(N)\leqslant\widetilde{\Psi}(N)\leqslant\Psi(N)+\sum_{t=1}^N\psi_{	au}(n_t)=\Psi(N)+O(1), \] so by changing $\psi$ to $\widetilde{\psi}$ we modify the right-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult} by $O(1)$. The term $O(1)$ is controlled by the error term in the right-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult}, so the claim is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Compare counts for $\psi$, $\widetilde\psi$, $\psi_\tau$; Theorem 6.5 makes the $\psi_\tau$ contribution $O(1)$.

nodes.name: Compare counting functions
nodes.statement: It follows from the definition~\eqref{def_cN} of the function $\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)$ that \[ \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)\leqslant \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\widetilde{\psi},N)\leqslant \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi,N)+\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{\tau},N) \]
nodes.statement_short: Counts for $\widetilde\psi$ are sandwiched by those for $\psi$ and $\psi_\tau$.

nodes.name: Apply the convergence theorem
nodes.statement: At the same time, it follows from~Theorem~\ref{mainCONV} that, for $\nu$-almost all pairs $({\alpha},{\gamma})$, we have $({\alpha}, {\gamma}) \notin \mathcal W(\psi_{\tau})$, which is equivalent to \[ \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{\tau},N) \ll 1, \]
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 6.5 makes the $\psi_\tau$ count bounded almost surely.

nodes.name: Left-hand side changes by O(1)
nodes.statement: Thus, $\nu$-almost surely, \[ \mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\widetilde{\psi},N)=\mathcal N({\alpha},{\gamma},\psi_{\tau},N) + O(1). \] For these pairs $(\alpha, {\gamma})$, when we change $\psi$ to $\widetilde{\psi}$, we modify the left-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult} by $O(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Changing $\psi$ to $\widetilde\psi$ changes the count by $O(1)$.

nodes.name: Right-hand side changes by O(1)
nodes.statement: Similarly, using the notation $\widetilde{\Psi}:=\sum_{t \leqslant N} \widetilde{\psi}(n_t)$, we have \[ \Psi(N)\leqslant\widetilde{\Psi}(N)\leqslant\Psi(N)+\sum_{t=1}^N\psi_{\tau}(n_t)=\Psi(N)+O(1), \] so by changing $\psi$ to $\widetilde{\psi}$ we modify the right-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult} by $O(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Psi$ changes by $O(1)$ since $\sum t^{-\tau}<\infty$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The term $O(1)$ is controlled by the error term in the right-hand side of \eqref{countlacresult}, so the claim is proved.
nodes.statement_short: $O(1)$ is absorbed by the error term.

nodes.name: Sum of nu(E_t)
nodes.statement:
Let $
u$ be a probability measure supported on a subset $F$ of $ [0,1)^2 $. Let $ (n_t)_{t\in \mathbb N} $ be a lacunary sequence of natural numbers such that $n_1 > 4$, and let $\psi:\mathbb{N}ightarrow [0,1/2)$. Suppose there exists a constant $A$ so that the measure $
u$ satisfies \eqref{LogDecay}. Then, for arbitrary $a,b \in \mathbb N$ with $a < b$, we have  egin{equation} \sum_{t=a}^b
u(\mathcal E_t) = 2\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \, + \, O\left( \min\Big(1,\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t)\Big) ight). \end{equation}
assumptions: $\nu$ be a probability measure supported on a subset $F$ of $ [0,1)^2 $
$ (n_t)_{t\in \mathbb N} $ be a lacunary sequence of natural numbers such that $n_1 > 4$
there exists a constant $A$ so that the measure $\nu$ satisfies \eqref{LogDecay}
nodes.label: lem_sum_mu_good

nodes.name: Equation (6.23)
nodes.statement: \sum_{t=a}^b\nu(\mathcal E_t) = 2\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \, + \, O\left( \min\Big(1,\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t)\Big) \right).
nodes.label: lem_sum_mu_good_result

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.8
nodes.statement_short: Fourier expansion of $W^\pm$ plus logarithmic decay, then the argument of PVZZ (69).

nodes.name: Fourier expansion
nodes.statement_short: Combine (6.12) with (6.5) and (6.8).

nodes.name: Use logarithmic decay
nodes.statement: By \eqref{LogDecay}, we have $| \widehat{\nu}(kn_t, -k)|\ll t^{-A},$ and combining this with \eqref{ub_single_sum} gives \begin{align*} \left| \sum_{t=a}^{b}\nu(\mathcal E_t) - 2\sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t) \right| \leqslant \sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t) \varepsilon_t + \sum_{t=a}^b\frac{O(1)}{t^{A}\sqrt{\varepsilon_t}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Logarithmic decay and Lemma 6.3 bound the Fourier terms.

nodes.name: Follow PVZZ
nodes.statement: This inequality is essentially the same as \cite[Equation (69)]{PVZZ2022}, and the arguments given there establish the claim.
nodes.statement_short: The argument of PVZZ (69) completes the proof.

nodes.name: Upper bound for nu of a pairwise intersection
nodes.statement: Observe from the definition that, for $s,t\in\mathbb{N}$, we have \begin{equation} \nu(\mathcal E_{s}\cap \mathcal E_{t}) \leqslant \int_{0}^{1} W_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^+({\alpha},\gamma) W_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^+({\alpha},\gamma) \, \mathrm{d}\nu({\alpha},\gamma). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation (6.24)
nodes.statement: \nu(\mathcal E_{s}\cap \mathcal E_{t}) \leqslant \int_{0}^{1} W_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^+({\alpha},\gamma) W_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^+({\alpha},\gamma) \, \mathrm{d}\nu({\alpha},\gamma).
nodes.label: ub_mu_first

nodes.name: Product function W_{s,t}
Equation (6.25)
nodes.label: Wst_Fourier

nodes.name: Zero coefficient of W_{s,t}
nodes.statement: Writing \[ {\lambda} \mathcal E_t = \{ ({\alpha}, {\gamma}) \in [0,1)^2: \| n_t {\alpha} - {\gamma} \| \leqslant {\lambda} \psi(n_t) \} \] for ${\lambda} > 1$ and $t \in \mathbb N$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \widehat{W}_{s,t}^+(0,0) &=\int_0^1\int_0^1 W_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^+({\alpha},\gamma)W_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^+({\alpha},\gamma) \mathrm d {\alpha} \mathrm d \gamma. \\&\leqslant\left| (1+\varepsilon_s)\mathcal E_s \cap (1+\varepsilon_t)\mathcal E_t \right| \\&= 4(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \\ &\qquad + O\left( (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big) \right), \end{aligned} \end{equation} where in the last step we have used \cite[Equation~(3.2.5)]{harman}.

nodes.name: Equation (6.26)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \widehat{W}_{s,t}^+(0,0) &=\int_0^1\int_0^1 W_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^+({\alpha},\gamma)W_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^+({\alpha},\gamma) \mathrm d {\alpha} \mathrm d \gamma. \\&\leqslant\left| (1+\varepsilon_s)\mathcal E_s \cap (1+\varepsilon_t)\mathcal E_t \right| \\&= 4(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \\ &\qquad + O\left( (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big) \right), \end{aligned}
nodes.label: main_q_Harman_ub2

nodes.name: Fourier sum for W_{s,t}
Equation (6.27)
nodes.label: Fourier_sum_principal

nodes.name: Bound for the sum S_{s,t}
nodes.statement: We denote by $S_{s,t}$ the sum in the right-hand side of~\eqref{Fourier_sum_principal}. Then, for any $s,t \in \mathbb{N}$ with $s < t$, \begin{equation} |S_{s,t}| \ll \frac{\psi(n_s)}{t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\, +\, \frac{\psi(n_t)}{s^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} \, + \, \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2} \varepsilon_t^{1/2}} \, + \ |T(s,t)|, \end{equation} where \begin{align} \notag &T(s,t) = \\ &\mathop{ \mathop{\sum\sum}_{ k,\ell\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus \{0\} } }_{ |kn_s+\ell n_t|<n_s^{1/2}} \!\!\! \what{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(kn_s,-k)\what{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell n_t,-\ell) \what{\nu}\left( -kn_s-\ell n_t,k+\ell\right). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bounds the off-zero Fourier sum $S_{s,t}$ by decay terms plus the near-resonant part $T(s,t)$.
nodes.label: prop_sum_S_m_n

nodes.name: Equation (6.28)
nodes.statement: |S_{s,t}| \ll \frac{\psi(n_s)}{t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\, +\, \frac{\psi(n_t)}{s^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} \, + \, \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2} \varepsilon_t^{1/2}} \, + \ |T(s,t)|,
nodes.label: S_bound

nodes.name: Equation (6.29)
nodes.statement: \notag &T(s,t) = \\ &\mathop{ \mathop{\sum\sum}_{ k,\ell\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus \{0\} } }_{ |kn_s+\ell n_t|<n_s^{1/2}} \!\!\! \what{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(kn_s,-k)\what{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell n_t,-\ell) \what{\nu}\left( -kn_s-\ell n_t,k+\ell\right).
nodes.label: def_S_prime

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.9
nodes.statement_short: Split $S_{s,t}$ into four ranges of $|kn_s+\ell n_t|$ and bound each with lacunarity and logarithmic decay.

nodes.name: Decompose S_{s,t}
nodes.statement_short: Split $S_{s,t}=S_1+S_2+S_3+T$ by the size of $|kn_s+\ell n_t|$.

nodes.name: Bound S_1
nodes.statement: To bound $S_1(s,t)$ from above, we first consider the terms with $\ell=0$. By the lacunarity of the sequence, and~\eqref{LogDecay}, \[ |\widehat{\nu}(-k n_s,k)|\ll \left(\log|kn_s|\right)^{-A}\ll |s|^{-A} \qquad (s \in \mathbb N). \] Together with~\eqref{fcoef_zero} and \eqref{ub_single_sum}, this implies that the sum $S_1(s,t)$ restricted to $\ell = 0$ is \[ \ll \ \frac{(2+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_t)}{|s|^{A}}\sum_{k\in \mathbb Z } \widehat{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(k n_s,-k) \ \ll \ \frac{\psi(n_t)}{|s|^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}}\, . \] A similar bound holds for the terms with $k=0$, and adding up we deduce that \begin{equation} S_1(s,t) \ll \frac{\psi(n_t)}{|s|^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} + \frac{\psi(n_s)}{|t|^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Terms with $k\ell=0$: logarithmic decay and Lemma 6.3.

nodes.name: Equation (6.30)
nodes.statement: S_1(s,t) \ll \frac{\psi(n_t)}{|s|^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} + \frac{\psi(n_s)}{|t|^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}.
nodes.label: ub_S1

nodes.name: Bound S_2
nodes.statement: For $S_2(s,t),$ the condition $|k n_s+\ell n_t|\geqslant n_t/2$, together with the lacunarity of the sequence, and \eqref{LogDecay}, gives \[ |\widehat{\nu}\left( -k n_s - \ell n_t,k+\ell\right)| \ll |t|^{-A}. \] This and \eqref{ub_double_sum} imply that \begin{equation} S_2(s,t) \ll \frac{1}{|t|^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Large frequencies: decay $\ll t^{-A}$ and (6.16).

nodes.name: Equation (6.31)
nodes.statement: S_2(s,t) \ll \frac{1}{|t|^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}.
nodes.label: ub_S2

nodes.name: Bound S_3
nodes.statement: For $S_3(s,t),$ the hypothesis $n_s^{1/2}\leqslant |k n_s+\ell n_t|< n_t/2$ together with the lacunarity of $(n_t)_{t\in \mathbb N}$ and~\eqref{LogDecay} gives \[ |\widehat{\nu}\left( -k n_s- \ell n_t, k+\ell \right)| \ll |s|^{-A}. \] Observe that under the condition of summation we have \[ |k n_s/n_t+\ell|< 1/2; \] this implies that for each $k$ there exists at most one index $\ell=\ell_k$ such that the pair $(k,\ell_k)$ satisfies the condition of summation. Moreover, the signs of $k$ and $\ell=\ell_k$ are necessarily opposite. These observations allow us to deduce the upper bound \begin{equation*} S_3(s,t) \ll \frac{1}{|s|^{A}} \mathop{\mathop{\sum}_{ k\in\mathbb N \, : } }_{\ell_k {\rm \, exists}} |\widehat{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(k n_s,-k)| \cdot |\widehat{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell_k n_t,-\ell_k) |. \end{equation*} We proceed by applying~\eqref{ub_Wpm_zero} to $\widehat{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell_k n_t,-\ell_k)$ and then the bound \eqref{ub_single_sum} to the sum $\sum\limits_{k\in\mathbb N}|\widehat{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(k n_s,-k)|$ to eventually get \vspace{-2mm} \begin{equation} S_3(s,t) \ll|s|^{-A}\psi(n_t)\varepsilon_s^{-1/2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Intermediate frequencies: at most one $\ell$ per $k$, then (6.13) and (6.15).

nodes.name: Equation (6.32)
nodes.statement: S_3(s,t) \ll|s|^{-A}\psi(n_t)\varepsilon_s^{-1/2}.
nodes.label: ub_S3

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{ub_S1}, \eqref{ub_S2} and~\eqref{ub_S3} yields the result.
nodes.statement_short: Add the three bounds.

nodes.name: General quasi-independence bound
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{indieMainThm}, let ${\theta} \in (0,1]$. Then, for any $a,b \in \mathbb{N}$ with $a < b$, we have \begin{multline} 2 \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \nu(\mathcal E_{s}\cap \mathcal E_{t}) \leqslant \left( \sum_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\right)^2 + O\left( \sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t) \right) \\ + O\Bigg(\left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)^{2-\theta}\!\!\!\log^+ \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)\,\, +\,\, \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}T(s,t) \\ + \,\, \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}(n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big) \Bigg). \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Pairwise-intersection bound with a free parameter $\theta$, error terms involving $T(s,t)$ and gcd sums.
conclusions: 2 \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \nu(\mathcal E_{s}\cap \mathcal E_{t}) \leqslant \left( \sum_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\right)^2 + O\left( \sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t) \right) \\ + O\Bigg(\left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)^{2-\theta}\!\!\!\log^+ \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)\,\, +\,\, \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}T(s,t) \\ + \,\, \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}(n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big) \Bigg). \end{multline}
nodes.label: indiethm_general

nodes.name: Equation (6.33)
nodes.statement: 2 \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \nu(\mathcal E_{s}\cap \mathcal E_{t}) \leqslant \left( \sum_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\right)^2 + O\left( \sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t) \right) \\ + O\Bigg(\left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)^{2-\theta}\!\!\!\log^+ \left(\sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t) \right)\,\, +\,\, \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}T(s,t) \\ + \,\, \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}(n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big) \Bigg).
nodes.label: ub_sum_eps_psipsi_combined

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.10
nodes.statement_short: Insert the $\varepsilon_t$ choice into the Fourier bounds and handle the error sums in two cases by the size of $\sum\psi(n_t)$.

nodes.name: Insert Fourier bounds
nodes.statement: By using the upper bound \eqref{ub_mu_first}, and then \eqref{main_q_Harman_ub2}, \eqref{S_bound} and Proposition~\ref{prop_sum_S_m_n} with \begin{equation} \varepsilon_t = \min\Bigg(2^{-\theta},\, \Big( \sum_{s=a}^{t}\psi(n_s) \Big)^{-\theta}\Bigg) \qquad (a \leqslant t \leqslant b), \end{equation} we find \begin{multline} 2 \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \nu(\mathcal E_{s}\cap \mathcal E_{t}) \leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \Bigg(4(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t)+\frac{\psi(n_s)}{t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\,\\ +\, \frac{\psi(n_t)}{s^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} \, + \, \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}+T(s,t)\Bigg)\\ + O\left(\mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big)\right). \end{multline}
nodes.statement_short: Apply (6.24), (6.26) and Proposition 6.9 with the choice (6.36) of $\varepsilon_t$.

nodes.name: Equation (6.34)
nodes.statement: \varepsilon_t = \min\Bigg(2^{-\theta},\, \Big( \sum_{s=a}^{t}\psi(n_s) \Big)^{-\theta}\Bigg) \qquad (a \leqslant t \leqslant b),
nodes.label: def_varepsilon_t

nodes.name: Equation (6.35)
nodes.statement: 2 \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \nu(\mathcal E_{s}\cap \mathcal E_{t}) \leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \Bigg(4(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t)+\frac{\psi(n_s)}{t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\,\\ +\, \frac{\psi(n_t)}{s^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} \, + \, \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}+T(s,t)\Bigg)\\ + O\left(\mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big)\right).
nodes.label: ub_sum_mu

nodes.name: Linear error terms
nodes.statement: It follows from \eqref{def_varepsilon_t} that \begin{equation} \varepsilon_t^{-1} \leqslant \max\left(2^{\theta},t^{\theta}\right) < 2t. \end{equation} Consequently $\sum\limits_{t=1}^{\infty}1/(t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}) <\infty,$ so we have the upper bound \begin{equation} \sum_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}\left(\frac{\psi(n_t)}{s^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} + \frac{\psi(n_s)}{t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\right) \ll \sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t) \end{equation} on part of the right-hand side of \eqref{ub_sum_mu}.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\varepsilon_t^{-1}<2t$, so the decay terms sum to $O(\sum\psi(n_t))$.

nodes.name: Equation (6.36)
nodes.statement: \varepsilon_t^{-1} \leqslant \max\left(2^{\theta},t^{\theta}\right) < 2t.
nodes.label: epsilon_inverse_bound

nodes.name: Equation (6.37)
nodes.statement: \sum_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b}\left(\frac{\psi(n_t)}{s^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} + \frac{\psi(n_s)}{t^{A}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\right) \ll \sum_{t=a}^b \psi(n_t)
nodes.label: ub_first_two_terms

nodes.name: Double sum of decay terms
nodes.statement: To bound the double sum $\sum\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} t^{-A}\varepsilon_s^{-1/2}\varepsilon_t^{-1/2}$ we consider two cases, according to whether $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)>2$ or $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\leqslant 2$. \noindent Case A: $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)>2$. In this case, \[ \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} \leqslant \frac{1}{t^{A}}\left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta}, \] and so \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}}\left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta} \\ &\ll \left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta}\leqslant \sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r). \end{aligned} \end{equation} \medskip \noindent Case B: $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\leqslant 2$. In this case, we have $\varepsilon_t=2^{-\theta}$ ($a\leqslant t\leqslant b$), so \[ \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\ll\frac{1}{t^{A}}. \] Applying Corollary~\ref{cor_min_psi} with $\tau = A/2$, we may assume that \[ \frac{1}{t^{A}}\leqslant\frac{\psi(n_t)}{t^{A/2}} \qquad (t \in \mathbb N), \] whence \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2} \varepsilon_t^{1/2}} &\ll \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} {\psi(n_t)}{t^{-A/2}} \\ &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} {\psi(n_t)}{s^{-A/2}} \ll \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t). \end{aligned} \end{equation} It follows from~\eqref{sum_const_leq_linear_case1} and~\eqref{sum_const_leq_linear_case2} that, in any case, \begin{equation} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\ll \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\sum t^{-A}\varepsilon_s^{-1/2}\varepsilon_t^{-1/2}$ in two cases.

nodes.name: Two cases
nodes.statement: To bound the double sum $\sum\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} t^{-A}\varepsilon_s^{-1/2}\varepsilon_t^{-1/2}$ we consider two cases, according to whether $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)>2$ or $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\leqslant 2$.
nodes.statement_short: Split according to whether $\sum\psi(n_t)>2$.

nodes.name: Case A
nodes.statement: Case A: $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)>2$. In this case, \[ \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} \leqslant \frac{1}{t^{A}}\left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta}, \] and so \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}}\left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta} \\ &\ll \left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta}\leqslant \sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r). \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Large sum: bound by $(\sum\psi)^\theta$.

nodes.name: Equation (6.38)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}}\left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta} \\ &\ll \left(\sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r)\right)^{\theta}\leqslant \sum_{r=a}^{b}\psi(n_r). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: sum_const_leq_linear_case1

nodes.name: Case B
nodes.statement: Case B: $\sum\limits_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\leqslant 2$. In this case, we have $\varepsilon_t=2^{-\theta}$ ($a\leqslant t\leqslant b$), so \[ \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\ll\frac{1}{t^{A}}. \] Applying Corollary~\ref{cor_min_psi} with $\tau = A/2$, we may assume that \[ \frac{1}{t^{A}}\leqslant\frac{\psi(n_t)}{t^{A/2}} \qquad (t \in \mathbb N), \] whence \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2} \varepsilon_t^{1/2}} &\ll \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} {\psi(n_t)}{t^{-A/2}} \\ &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} {\psi(n_t)}{s^{-A/2}} \ll \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t). \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Small sum: use Corollary 6.7 with $\tau=A/2$.

nodes.name: Equation (6.39)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2} \varepsilon_t^{1/2}} &\ll \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} {\psi(n_t)}{t^{-A/2}} \\ &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} {\psi(n_t)}{s^{-A/2}} \ll \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: sum_const_leq_linear_case2

nodes.name: Either case
nodes.statement: It follows from~\eqref{sum_const_leq_linear_case1} and~\eqref{sum_const_leq_linear_case2} that, in any case, \begin{equation} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\ll \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: In any case the double sum is $\ll\sum\psi(n_t)$.

nodes.name: Equation (6.40)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \frac{1}{t^{A}\varepsilon_s^{1/2}\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\ll \sum_{t=a}^b\psi(n_t).
nodes.label: sum_const_leq_linear

nodes.name: Main term
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\sum(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi\psi$ in two cases.

nodes.name: Expand the main term
nodes.statement: We now proceed to estimate the first term on the right-hand side of~\eqref{ub_sum_mu}. To this end, we will make use of~\eqref{main_q_Harman_ub2}. With this in mind, first note that by definition $t \mapsto \varepsilon_t$ is non-increasing, so \[ \varepsilon_t \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t) \leqslant \varepsilon_s \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t) \] whenever $s < t$. Moreover, we have $\varepsilon_t \leqslant 1$ for all $t\in\mathbb N$, and so \[ \varepsilon_s \varepsilon_t \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t) \leqslant \varepsilon_s \psi(n_s)\psi(n_t). \] Thus \begin{equation} 4(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \, \leqslant \, 4\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) + 12 \varepsilon_s \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t). \end{equation} We estimate the sum of the second term on the right-hand side of \eqref{sum_eps_psipsi_developed} by considering two cases, A and B as above.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity of $\varepsilon_t$ gives (6.42); split the $\varepsilon_s$ term into two cases.

nodes.name: Equation (6.41)
nodes.statement: 4(1+\varepsilon_s)(1+\varepsilon_t)\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \, \leqslant \, 4\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) + 12 \varepsilon_s \psi(n_s) \psi(n_t).
nodes.label: sum_eps_psipsi_developed

nodes.name: Case A
nodes.statement_short: Use PVZZ Lemma D2 to get a $(\sum\psi)^{2-\theta}\log$ bound.

nodes.name: Equation (6.42)
nodes.statement:
otag &\mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \varepsilon_s\psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) \ 
otag &= \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} \psi(n_s)\psi(n_t)\ \min\Bigg(2^{-	heta}, \left( \sum_{r=a}^{s}\psi(n_r) ight)^{-	heta} \Bigg) \

nodes.label: ub_sum_eps_psipsi

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 6.2
nodes.statement: By employing Proposition~\ref{indiethm_general} with $\theta=2/3$, we find that it is enough to provide upper bounds for the sums \begin{equation*} \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big) \end{equation*} and \begin{equation} \mathop{\sum\sum}\limits_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} T(s,t), \end{equation} where $T(s,t)$ is given by \eqref{def_S_prime}. We now carry this out. First, using the fact that $(n_t)_{t\in\mathbb N}$ is a lacunary sequence, we find \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} (n_s,n_t)\min\Big(\frac{\psi(n_s)}{n_s},\frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\Big) &\leqslant \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s<t\leqslant b} n_s \frac{\psi(n_t)}{n_t}\\ =\sum_{t=a+1}^b \psi(n_t)\sum_{a\leqslant s < t}\frac{n_s}{n_t} &\ll \sum_{t=a+1}^b \psi(n_t). \end{aligned} \end{equation*} Next, we are going to find a suitable upper bound for the sum~\eqref{sum_Tst}. Recall that $T(s,t)$ is the sum of terms \[ \what{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(kn_s,-k)\what{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell n_t,-\ell) \what{\nu}\left( -kn_s-\ell n_t,k+\ell\right), \] over non-zero integers $k,\ell$ for which \begin{equation} |k n_s-\ell n_t|< n_s^{1/2}, \end{equation} where $\varepsilon_a, \ldots, \varepsilon_b$ are given by~\eqref{def_varepsilon_t}. By dividing both sides of~\eqref{condition_T} by $n_s$, we get \begin{equation} |k -\ell n_t/n_s|< 1. \end{equation} Hence, if $k$ and $\ell$ satisfy \eqref{index_restriction_first_boundsv} then they must have the same sign. Further, for each fixed integer $\ell$, there exists a set $S_{\ell}$ of at most two non-zero integers $k$ satisfying \eqref{index_restriction_first_boundsv}. On using the trivial bound $|\what{\nu}(k_1,k_2)| \leqslant 1 $, it follows that $$ |T(s,t)| \leqslant 2 \mathop{\mathop{\sum}_{ k, \ell \in \mathbb N} }_{k \in S_{\ell}} |\what{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(k n_s,-k) \what{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell n_t,-\ell) |. $$ Note from \eqref{index_restriction_first_boundsv} and the inequality $\left|\ell n_t/n_s\right| > 1$ that \begin{equation} \frac12 \frac{n_s}{n_t} k \leqslant \frac{n_s}{n_t} \max \{1, k-1 \} \, \leqslant \, \ell\, \leqslant \frac{n_s}{n_t} (k+1)\leqslant 2\frac{n_s}{n_t} k. \end{equation} Using \eqref{W_ub_psi} to bound $\what{W}_{n_t,\varepsilon_t}^{+}(\ell n_t,-\ell)$, and using \eqref{W_ub_psi}, \eqref{W_ub_1s2} and \eqref{ratio} to bound $\what{W}_{n_s,\varepsilon_s}^{+}(k n_s,-k) $, yields \begin{eqnarray*} |T(s,t)| &\ll & \sum_{\ell \in \mathbb{N} } \ \min\left(\frac{n_s^2}{n_t^2}\cdot\frac{1}{\ell^2\psi(n_s)\varepsilon_s},\psi(n_s)\right)\psi(n_t)\\[2ex] &\ll& \sum_{\ell \leqslant \frac{n_s}{n_t\psi(n_s)\varepsilon_s^{1/2}}} \hspace{-5mm} \psi(n_s)\psi(n_t) + \sum_{\ell > \frac{n_s}{n_t\psi(n_s)\varepsilon_s^{1/2}}} \frac{n_s^2}{n_t^2}\cdot \frac{\psi(n_t)}{\ell^2\psi(n_s) \varepsilon_s}\\[2ex] &\ll& \frac{n_s}{n_t}\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\varepsilon_s^{1/2}} \leqslant \ \frac{n_s}{n_t}\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}. \end{eqnarray*} The last inequality makes use of the fact that $t \mapsto \varepsilon_t$ is non-increasing. By lacunarity, we have \[ \sum\limits_{1\leqslant s<t}n_s/n_t \ll 1. \] Consequently, if $a,b \in \mathbb{N}$ with $a < b$, then \[ \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s < t\leqslant b} T(s,t) \ll \sum_{t=a}^b\sum_{s=a}^{t-1}\frac{n_s}{n_t}\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\varepsilon_t^{1/2}} \ll \sum_{t=a}^{b}\frac{\psi(n_t)}{\varepsilon_t^{1/2}}\, . \] Finally, recalling that the $\varepsilon_t$ are given by \eqref{def_varepsilon_t}, we obtain the upper bound \[ \mathop{\sum\sum}_{a\leqslant s < t\leqslant b} T(s,t) \ll \left(\sum_{t=a}^{b}\psi(n_t)\right)^{1+\theta/2}. \] The choice $\theta=2/3$ delivers \eqref{delta_set_frac23}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 6.10 with $\theta=2/3$; bound the gcd sum and $T(s,t)$ by lacunarity.

We now carry this out.
nodes.statement_short: With $\theta=2/3$ it suffices to bound the gcd sum and $\sum T(s,t)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.15
nodes.statement: Having established Theorem~\ref{GeneralCountingThm}, we now infer Theorem~\ref{GeneralMultThmQ}. Given $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}$ and $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$, we set \[ C = \sup \left\{ \frac{1}{t} \log q_t(\alpha): t \in \mathbb N \right\} > 0. \] Let $(n_t)_{t\in \mathbb N} \subseteq \mathbb N$ be a lacunary sequence such that \begin{equation} \|n_t\alpha - \gamma\| \leqslant \frac{8}{n_t} \qquad (t\geqslant 1) \end{equation} and \begin{equation} 8^t<n_t\leqslant 4e^{6Ct}. \end{equation} The existence of such a sequence is shown in \cite[Lemma 2.1]{CZ2021}. We now define an approximating function $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to [0,1]$ by setting $\psi(1)=0$ and \[ \psi(n) = \frac{1}{8 \log n} \qquad (n \geqslant 2). \] Then, for $N\in\mathbb N$, \[ \Psi(N)=\sum_{t=1}^N\psi(n_t)\asymp \log N. \] By Theorem~\ref{GeneralCountingThm}, there exists $\mathcal B_1 \subseteq \mathcal B$ of Hausdorff dimension $2$ such that, for all $(\beta,\delta)\in \mathcal B_1$ and all $t\in\mathbb N$, we have \begin{equation} \mathcal N(\beta,\delta,\psi,t)\asymp\Psi(t)\asymp\log t. \end{equation} Given $T\in\mathbb N$, define $t\in\mathbb N$ by \[ n_t\leqslant T < n_{t+1}. \] By~\eqref{n_t_is_exponential}, we have $T\asymp n_t$ and $t\asymp\log T$. At the same time, by~\eqref{GeneralMultThmQ_asymp_cN}, there exist $\asymp \log t$ indices $1\leqslant s\leqslant t$ such that \begin{equation} \|n_s\beta - \delta\| \leqslant\frac{1}{8\log n_s}. \end{equation} Multiplying~\eqref{nt_rate} and~\eqref{secondary_rate_n_s} we get that, for all such indices $s$, the inequality~\eqref{strong_Littlewood_ie} holds with $n=n_s\leqslant n_t\leqslant T$. Therefore, \[ \widetilde{\mathcal N}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta,T)\gg \log t\asymp \log\log T, \] which proves the claim of Theorem~\ref{GeneralMultThmQ}.
nodes.statement_short: Pick a lacunary sequence of good approximations for $(\alpha,\gamma)$ and $\psi(n)=1/(8\log n)$; Theorem 1.9 supplies $\asymp\log t$ good indices for $(\beta,\delta)$.

nodes.name: Growth constant C
nodes.statement: Having established Theorem~\ref{GeneralCountingThm}, we now infer Theorem~\ref{GeneralMultThmQ}. Given $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}$ and $\gamma\in\mathbb{R}$, we set \[ C = \sup \left\{ \frac{1}{t} \log q_t(\alpha): t \in \mathbb N \right\} > 0. \]
nodes.statement_short: Set $C=\sup t^{-1}\log q_t(\alpha)$.

nodes.name: Choose the lacunary sequence
nodes.statement: Let $(n_t)_{t\in \mathbb N} \subseteq \mathbb N$ be a lacunary sequence such that \begin{equation} \|n_t\alpha - \gamma\| \leqslant \frac{8}{n_t} \qquad (t\geqslant 1) \end{equation} and \begin{equation} 8^t<n_t\leqslant 4e^{6Ct}. \end{equation} The existence of such a sequence is shown in \cite[Lemma 2.1]{CZ2021}.

At the same time, by~\eqref{GeneralMultThmQ_asymp_cN}, there exist $\asymp \log t$ indices $1\leqslant s\leqslant t$ such that \begin{equation} \|n_s\beta - \delta\| \leqslant\frac{1}{8\log n_s}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Multiply the bounds

Therefore, \[ \widetilde{\mathcal N}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta,T)\gg \log t\asymp \log\log T, \] which proves the claim of Theorem~\ref{GeneralMultThmQ}.
